blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infusion pump free-flow prevention
stem: What is the safety purpose of an anti-free-flow mechanism in an IV infusion administration set?

options.A: Prevent uncontrolled gravity flow of IV fluid or medication when the set is removed from active pump control or the pump door is opened.
options.B: Increase the infusion rate automatically when downstream resistance rises so the prescribed volume is delivered on schedule.
options.C: Eliminate the need to monitor the pump and patient because uncontrolled flow cannot occur when an anti-free-flow component is present.
options.D: Convert the IV administration set for enteral use when the infusion pump is unavailable, allowing gravity delivery through the same tubing.

rationale: A is correct. FDA infusion-pump safety materials identify uncontrolled infusate flow or free flow as a hazardous situation that can cause over-infusion. FDA-cleared infusion administration sets describe a free-flow protection clamp intended to prevent free flow when the pump door is opened and the set is removed. B would worsen an occlusion-related hazard rather than prevent free flow. C falsely suggests monitoring is unnecessary. D describes unsafe cross-route use unrelated to anti-free-flow design.
educational_objective: Explain that anti-free-flow mechanisms reduce the risk of uncontrolled gravity infusion and over-infusion when administration tubing is no longer actively controlled by the pump.
source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA); NCSBN
source_document_title: Infusion Pumps; Infusion Pump Total Product Life Cycle Guidance; FDA-cleared Infusomat Space Volumetric Infusion Pump Administration Sets; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Current FDA infusion-pump pages live-rechecked 2026-08-21; FDA 510(k) K243392 issued 2025 and current in FDA database; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: FDA Infusion Pump Total Product Life Cycle Guidance, operational hazards: uncontrolled flow of infusate/free flow can result from delivery-path failures or unintended gravity flow. FDA K243392 510(k) summary: administration sets contain a free-flow protection clamp intended to prevent free flow when the pump door is opened and the set is removed. Current FDA clinician risk-reduction page also emphasizes preventing over-infusion during pump failure.
source_claim_supported: FDA evidence directly supports anti-free-flow design as protection against uncontrolled gravity flow and associated over-infusion risk when tubing is removed from pump control.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe use of equipment and prevention of medication-administration injury.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — relevant official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan safety content was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; pump-mechanism claims rely on FDA web/database evidence.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches the FDA-described function of free-flow protection.
option_audit.B: Plausible flow-control misconception but increased rate during resistance is not the purpose and could create harm.
option_audit.C: Plausible device-reliance misconception but anti-free-flow design does not eliminate monitoring requirements.
option_audit.D: Plausible equipment-substitution misconception but cross-route conversion is unrelated and unsafe.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are comparable in detail and structure; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
